Min: Quick update — ran activation-preconditioning experiments (SmoothQuant-style) combined with AWQ/GPTQ on the 13B long-form model (32k context). Dropping a quick summary and config so folks can reproduce.
Alex: Nice, interested in baseline numbers first.
Min: Baseline FP16 (no quant) throughput ~14 tok/s at 32k with median chunk latency ~220ms. Eval perplexity on our longdoc set: 12.3.
Alex: OK. How do the quant methods compare?
Min: AWQ int8 alone: throughput ~21 tok/s, PPL 12.8 (+4.1% relative). GPTQ 4-bit: throughput ~28 tok/s, PPL 13.9 (+12.6%) and we observed degradation on numeric reasoning & table extraction tasks.
Dalia: What about adding activation preconditioning (SmoothQuant-ish)?
Min: SmoothQuant-style preconditioning + AWQ int8: throughput ~23 tok/s, PPL 12.4 (+0.8%). So preconditioning recovers most of the PPL regression from plain AWQ. Peak GPU memory dropped ~18% vs FP16. KV cache memory unchanged.
Rohit: Any long-context-specific failure modes at 32k?
Min: Two things: (1) layers with heavy activation scale early in sequence cause large per-channel outliers; SmoothQuant reduces those. (2) GPTQ 4-bit occasionally hit numeric instability after ~20k tokens — appears as attention matmul overflow; we mitigated partially with per-op clipping but it's brittle.
Alex: Can you paste the quant command/config you used?
Min: Sure — reproducible smoke-run command:
```bash
python quantize.py --model 13b-longctx --scheme activation_precond --quant awq --bits 8 --calib-n 2000 --clip 0.98 --out 13b_awq_actprecond
```
Notes: calibration used 2k samples drawn from our long-doc corpus, activation scales used per-channel for linear layers and per-tensor for embeddings.
Dalia: Any downstream eval numbers (QA/hallucination)?
Min: Quick retrieval-QA hit rates: FP16 0.64, AWQ 0.59, AWQ+act-precond 0.63. Hallucination metrics follow same recovery pattern. We also ran a small rouge/EM sweep on summarization slices — AWQ+precond was within 1-2% of FP16.
Rohit: Deployment recommendations (Hosted vs Dedicated)?
Min: Hosted: AWQ+activation-precond int8 looks like best cost/quality tradeoff — recommend enabling auto-fallback to FP16 when latency SLOs or eval drift triggers. Dedicated: for customers prioritizing throughput, GPTQ 4-bit is possible behind conservative A/B rollout and extra clipping, but not for numeric-heavy workloads. For regulated workloads, default to AWQ+precond.
quant-bot: job 67382 finished — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-quant/13b_awq_actprecond/1745003210/
Alex: Can you open a PR to add this profile to model-profiles (include calib params and clip) and wire a nightly eval focusing on long-context numeric reasoning?
Min: Will do. Also running a 10k calib sweep tonight across clip values [0.95,0.98,0.99] and posting full plots tomorrow. Uploading preview plots: https://internal.redwood.ai/plots/13b_awq_actprecond
Dalia: Awesome. @Min ping when the sweep finishes :thumbsup:
Min: Yep — sweep scheduled for tonight, will post final numbers tomorrow morning.
